findings.summary: Every page's title names the small tail-end section it opens with rather than the material that fills it, so all four titles misdescribe their page by roughly one chapter.
findings.evidence: Page 1 is titled "N+1, DataLoader, Performance" but after the opening "Caching And Measuring" block it runs "What A Throw Produces", "Null Propagation", "null Or Throw", "What Reaches The Client"; page 2 is titled "Errors, Nullability, Return Shapes" but after two error blocks it runs "Picking A Concrete Type", "Subscriptions Have Two", "Directives Wrap Resolvers", "Scalars And Enums"; page 3 is titled "Interfaces, Unions, Subscriptions" but after one federation sidebox it runs "The Whole Thing, Short" and "What Actually Breaks".
findings.fix: Retitle each page after its dominant content (page 1 "Errors and Nullability", page 2 "Interfaces, Unions, Subscriptions, Directives", page 3 "Federation and the Recap"), or move the carried-over tail blocks back onto the preceding page so title and body agree.

findings.summary: The null-propagation table's `[Post!]!` row is wrong: a non-null list cannot itself become null, so the error propagates past the list to the nearest nullable ancestor.
findings.fix: Change the row to `[Post!]` → "one bad element nulls the whole list", and add/replace `[Post!]!` → "one bad element nulls the nearest nullable ancestor above the list".

findings.summary: In the "Result union" comparison box the inline code `User | NotFoundError` overflows the box's right border instead of wrapping inside it.
findings.evidence: The bullet dot for the item renders alone on one line and the token "User | NotFoundError" then runs to the box's pink right border (~x=1016 on a 1080px-wide page), with "NotFoundError" touching/crossing the border, while the neighbouring "Throw" box's lines all end well inside their frame.
findings.fix: Allow the comparison-column inline code to break (word-break/overflow-wrap on code spans inside comparison cells) or shorten the line in data/handbooks/graphql/resolvers/parts/02/post.json:115 to e.g. `User | NotFound`.

findings.summary: The subscription code example's `resolve` is identical to the default resolver the bullets just described, so its `// else null` comment claims a fix that changes nothing.
findings.evidence: Bullet: "No explicit `resolve()`: the default reads `payload[fieldName]`" alongside code: "resolve: p => p.messageAdded,  // else null"
findings.fix: Show the actual mismatch case: publish the raw object (`pubsub.publish('MSG', message)`) and write `resolve: p => p,  // payload is the message itself, not { messageAdded }` — or keep the wrapped publish and drop the redundant `resolve` line.

findings.summary: The page states __typename does not come from the returned value and then, three blocks later, tells the reader to put __typename on the returned row and read it.
findings.evidence: Sidebox "Two Quiet Traps": "`__typename` comes from the schema, not your return shape" — followed by the code block "`__resolveType: row => row.__typename,`  // cheapest: put it on the row".
findings.fix: Distinguish the two cases in the sidebox: the response's `__typename` field is derived by the executor from the schema/`__resolveType` and cannot be forged by returning it; carrying a private `__typename` on the row is only an input your own `__resolveType` reads.
Run the fit pass — it adds material from the book without removing anything.

findings.summary: The heading "3. Three Trade-Offs" sits alone at the bottom of page 3 with no content under it and the entire lower half of the page blank, its table appearing only on page 4.
findings.evidence: Page 3 ends with "→ 3. Three Trade-Offs" directly above the "#dev #notes 3/4" footer; the matching "choice / what it costs" table is the first block on page 4. post.json page 3 blocks end with {"type":"heading","text":"Three Trade-Offs"} (line 365-367).
findings.fix: Move the trailing heading block to the start of page 4 in post.json so it stays with its table (or keep headings and their following block together during pagination).
Run the fit pass — it adds material from the book without removing anything.

findings.summary: Page titles are offset from their content: each page's heading describes the topics of the following page.
findings.evidence: Page 1 is titled "N+1, DataLoader, Performance" but its bulk is "What A Throw Produces"/"Null Propagation"/"null Or Throw"; page 2 is titled "Errors, Nullability, Return Shapes" but covers `__resolveType`, subscriptions and directives; page 3 is titled "Interfaces, Unions, Subscriptions" but covers federation and "What Actually Breaks".
findings.fix: Shift each `page_title` back one page so titles match the blocks they head (p1 → DataLoader + errors intro, p2 → "Errors, Nullability, Return Shapes" content, p3 → "Interfaces, Unions, Subscriptions", p4 → "Traps, Trade-Offs"), or move the blocks to match the existing titles.

findings.summary: The caption advertises a page count and topics that belong to Part 1, so a reader arriving at this part expects sections it does not contain.
findings.evidence: Caption: "Ten pages on the four arguments, the default resolver that quietly runs most of your schema, why root mutations are the spec's only ordering guarantee" — the part has four pages and covers none of the four arguments, defaults, or mutation ordering except as one recap bullet.
findings.fix: Rewrite the caption to describe this part's actual arc (caching and measuring, errors and nullability, abstract types, subscriptions, directives, the recap) and correct the page count to four.

findings.summary: The caption's first sentence is a bare series label with no hook, burying the actual hook in the second sentence.
findings.evidence: "Part 2 of GRAPHQL INTERNALS. Your resolver returned an object and the next resolver got it — that one sentence is the entire GraphQL execution model..."
findings.fix: Lead with the hook and move the part label later or into the series field: "Your resolver returned an object and the next resolver got it — that one sentence is the entire GraphQL execution model, and almost every bug you will ship is a corollary of it. Part 2 of GRAPHQL INTERNALS: ten pages on..."

findings.summary: The null-propagation table contrasts `[Post]` with `[Post!]!` without ever stating that the inner `!` is what decides element-nulling versus list-nulling.
findings.evidence: Table rows: ["`[Post]`","only that element nulls"] and ["`[Post!]!`","one bad element nulls the list"], with no row for `[Post]!` and no bullet explaining inner vs outer `!`.
findings.fix: Add a `[Post]!` row ("element nulls, list survives") and one bullet stating the rule: the inner `!` governs the element, the outer `!` governs the list.

findings.summary: `pubsub.iterator()` is not a method on graphql-subscriptions' PubSub — the API is `asyncIterator()` (deprecated) / `asyncIterableIterator()` / `asyncIterable()`.
findings.fix: Use `pubsub.asyncIterableIterator('MSG')` (current graphql-subscriptions v3+ name; `asyncIterator` is the deprecated older spelling).

findings.summary: The directives section asserts that the outermost wrapper runs first without showing how SDL directive order maps to wrapping order, leaving the rule unusable.
findings.evidence: "Several directives on one field: the outermost runs first" and "Order of application decides who sees the raw value" — no example of a field carrying two directives.
findings.fix: Add a two-line example (e.g. `field: String @auth @upper`) and state explicitly which of the two ends up outermost and therefore runs first.

findings.summary: The first bullet of the "Across Services" side box renders as a bare "-" marker with an empty line, its text pushed to the next line.
findings.evidence: The box shows "-" alone on its own line followed by "__resolveReference(ref, ctx, info) resolves an entity from key fields" on the lines below, unlike the following two bullets whose markers sit on the same line as their text.
findings.fix: Let the leading inline-code token wrap within the bullet line (overflow-wrap/break on code spans in sidebox items) so `__resolveReference(ref, ctx, info)` starts on the marker's line.

findings.summary: The heading "Three Trade-Offs" is the last block on page 3 while the table it labels is the first block on page 4, orphaning the heading from its content.
findings.evidence: Page 3 ends with {"type":"heading","text":"Three Trade-Offs"}; page 4 begins with the table headed ["Choice","What it costs"].
findings.fix: Move the "Three Trade-Offs" heading to the top of page 4 immediately above its table, or pull the table up onto page 3 beneath the heading.
